result.label: Source-read

claims.claim: Under §473(b), the court may relieve a party from a judgment, dismissal, order, or other proceeding on terms that are just.
claims.quote: (b) The court may, upon any terms as may be just, relieve a party or the party’s legal representative from a judgment, dismissal, order, or other proceeding

claims.claim: The judgment, dismissal, order, or proceeding must have been taken against the party through the party’s mistake, inadvertence, surprise, or excusable neglect.
claims.quote: taken against the party through the party’s mistake, inadvertence, surprise, or excusable neglect.
claims.note: These are alternative grounds for the discretionary relief described.

claims.claim: The application must include a copy of the answer or other pleading proposed to be filed.
claims.quote: Application for this relief shall be accompanied by a copy of the answer or other pleading proposed to be filed therein, otherwise the application shall not be granted

claims.claim: The application must be made within a reasonable time.
claims.quote: and shall be made within a reasonable time, in no case exceeding six months
claims.note: Filing within six months does not by itself establish reasonableness.

claims.claim: Six months after the judgment, dismissal, order, or proceeding was taken is the outer limit for that application.
claims.quote: in no case exceeding six months, after the judgment, dismissal, order, or proceeding was taken.

claims.claim: Under §473(a)(1), the court has discretion to allow a late answer after notice to the adverse party.
claims.quote: The court may likewise, in its discretion, after notice to the adverse party, allow, upon any terms as may be just, an amendment to any pleading or proceeding in other particulars; and may upon like terms allow an answer to be made after the time limited by this code.
claims.note: The court may impose just terms.

claims.claim: Under §473(d), either party may move to set aside a void judgment or order; after notice to the other party, the court may grant that relief.
claims.quote: and may, on motion of either party after notice to the other party, set aside any void judgment or order.

claims.claim: The current version remains in effect through December 31, 2026.
claims.quote: (e) This section shall remain in effect only until January 1, 2027, and as of that date is repealed.

claims.claim: The replacement version becomes operative January 1, 2027.
claims.quote: (f) This section shall become operative on January 1, 2027.

claims.claim: Subdivisions (a) through (d) retain the same wording.
claims.note: The supplied statutory texts match in those subdivisions.

claims.claim: A new subdivision (e) replaces the repeal provision.
claims.quote: The old subdivision (e) (repeal on January 1, 2027) is replaced by a new (e) on motions to vacate a default judgment void for lack of proper service

claims.claim: New subdivision (e) allows a party to move to vacate a default judgment that is void for lack of proper service.
claims.quote: a party to an action may bring a motion to vacate a default judgment that is void for lack of proper service

claims.claim: Under the new provision, that motion may be brought at any time after entry of the judgment.
claims.quote: a default judgment that is void for lack of proper service at any time after entry of the judgment.
claims.note: This timing rule is specific to the motion described in new subdivision (e).

flags.text: The express “at any time after entry” provision for a default judgment void for lack of proper service becomes operative January 1, 2027. It does not change subdivision (b)’s reasonable-time requirement or six-month ceiling.

result.summary: The claims are supported within the stated scope. The draft distinguishes the current discretionary-relief deadline from the timing provision that becomes operative in 2027.
